newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore share index marks time ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: Singapore share index marks time ahead of weekend.

text.p: Singapore shares ended almost unchanged on Thursday as dealers squared books ahead of a long weekend. Most Singapore markets were due to be closed on Friday for a Moslem religious festival.

The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) closed up 3.01 points at 2,043.20 -- still hovering just above the 25-month low of 2,027.11 hit in intraday trading on Tuesday. Volume was 152.9 million shares with 206 gainers and 134 losers.
"Apart from the new issues, there was very little volume," said one dealer. "We're still looking to Wall Street for direction for next week."
New issues grabbed much of the interest and new listings MMI Holdings and Raffles Medical were the two most active stocks.

Disk drive maker MMI Holdings, which debuted on Wednesday, rose seven cents to S$0.61 on 23.1 million shares while healthcare company Raffles Medical Group, which began trading last week, rose four cents to S$0.58 on 12.1 million shares.

Shares in property and steel company Lion Teck Chiang began their first day of trading at Singapore $1.30 each, unchanged from their initial public offer price. They rose to a high of S$1.38 but later slipped back to S$1.34 on 2.3 million shares.
